newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FOCUS-WMC YEAR PROFIT SOFTENS WITH METALS.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-WMC YEAR PROFIT SOFTENS WITH METALS.

text.p: Resources group WMC Ltd, hit by weak base precious metal prices, reported its first fall in operating earnings in four years on Wednesday.

The company said earnings before tax and abnormals fell to A$252.7 million in the year to June 30 from A$520.1 million the previous year. But the pre-abnormals net figure of A$228.2 million was at the upper end of analysts' forecast range of A$195 million to A$240 million.
After tax earnings of A$297.2 million were boosted by an abnormal gain of A$40.5 million after the company sold most of its petroleum assets during the year.
WMC said its nickel division was worst affected by metal price falls. Pre-tax earnings in the unit fell to A$130.6 million from A$314.9 million.
Operating profit from alumina fell to A$258.5 million from A$299.6 million, gold to A$41.6 million from A$63.6 million and copper/uranium to A$83.5 million from A$123.1 million.
WMC shares bounced from a low of A$7.29 before the result was announced to close one cent weaker at A$7.41.
The resource group's shares have been very weak in the lead-up to the annual results, dropping about 16 percent since late June when they touched a high of A$8.80.

"The result seems reasonable given lower metal prices and the problems it had with its nickel smelter earlier this year. I would expect the shares to continue to recover," a Sydney based resources analyst told Reuters.

A furnace roof collapse at WMC's nickel smelter in Western Australia and interruptions to the copper smelter at the Olympic Dam mine in South Australia due to an acid plant expansion both contributed to higher costs during the year.

At a media briefing to discuss the results, WMC managing director Hugh Morgan said it was too early to give confident profit predictions but tipped higher base metal output and lower costs for the group in 1997/98.

"In terms of volume, there should be more metal produced. The major change this year is we don't expect to have any interruptions for nickel production which should be running at its full capacity," Morgan said.
Morgan said gold production would be lower due to the sale of the high cost Hill 50 mine in Western Australia.
Although alumina prices were currently not much different than in the previous financal year, Morgan said WMC saw an upward trend emerging.
In respect of costs, Morgan said WMC expected improvements for its gold and alumina operations and a much better performance from its nickel business.
Morgan said the group's relatively low gearing level of about 21 percent meant it would not need to access equity markets to help fund its current expansion plans.
"We have a committment to grow the company but the focus of growth at the moment is making sure these very large projects that we have in train come to fruition properly."
WMC has commenced a A$1.48 billion expansion of the Olympic Dam copper/uranium mine which aims to double the level of production to 200,000 tonnes or ore by 2001.
The company is also in the process of developing a A$750 million fertiliser project at Phosphate Hill in Queensland.
